content: Activating transcription factor 5, commonly referred to as ATF5, is a protein encoded by the ATF5 gene in humans. ATF5 was first characterized by Nishizawa and Nagata and is classified as a member of the activating transcription factor (ATF) and cAMP response-element binding protein (CREB) family. The expression of ATF5 transcripts and protein occurs across a wide range of tissues, with particularly high levels of transcript expression observed in the liver. ATF5 is also found in various types of tumor cells. The regulation of ATF5 expression occurs at both the transcriptional and translational levels. During brain development, ATF5 is expressed in the ventricular zone (VZ) and subventricular zone (SVZ). The human ATF5 protein consists of 282 amino acids. ATF5 functions as a transcription factor and contains a basic leucine zipper (bZip) domain.
